title: Operating Lines of Credit Advance Hold Following a Recent Returned Payment
content:
A payment on one of the Operating Lines of Credit that came back unpaid within the past month places a hold on part of what the line will advance.

## Rule

The figure — what remains of the lending limit once everything to be taken off it has been taken off — is taken:

- **at 0.5 of itself** when a payment on the line came back unpaid within one whole month before today and two or more did in the twelve whole months before today;
- **at 0.75 of itself** when one came back within one whole month before today and fewer than two did in the twelve months;
- **at the whole of itself** when none came back within one whole month before today.

Payments that came back unpaid are the returned interest payments and returned principal payments in the line's transaction history. The share applies before the result is compared with the room left on the day's phone limit and rounded to cents.

## Combinations

| Returned within one whole month before today | Returned in the twelve whole months before today (the recent one included) | Share of the figure |
|---|---|---|
| One or more | Two or more | 0.5 |
| One | One | 0.75 |
| None | Any number | Whole |

## Illustration (hypothetical figure of USD 80,000.00)

With one payment returned last week and another returned five months ago, the figure is taken at 0.5 of itself, USD 40,000.00; with only the payment returned last week, at 0.75 of itself, USD 60,000.00; with only the payment returned five months ago, at the whole USD 80,000.00.
